❯ In one sentence, what is a Neovim terminal buffer? Do not use any tools.                                                                                              

● 1. :checkhealth: runs diagnostics on Neovim and plugins and reports problems.
  2. Extmark: a mark on a buffer position that moves with edits, used for highlights and virtual text.
  3. chansend(): sends data to a channel, such as a job's or terminal's stdin.
  4. Bracketed paste: the terminal wraps pasted text in escape codes so apps don't treat it as typed keys.

❯ @lua/floating-claude/state.lua#L1-10 In one sentence, what do these lines say?                                                                                        
  ⎿  Read lua/floating-claude/state.lua (10 lines)

● These lines begin a shared state table holding the live Claude Code terminal's handles. They are its buffer, its float window and its job ID, plus the buffer of the
  minimized corner window that shows the latest message. Each starts at -1, meaning not open yet.

❯ @lua/floating-claude/state.lua#L12-14 Answer in one sentence:                                                                                                         
  what are these lines for?                                                                                                                                             
  Do not use any tools.                                                                                                                                                 
  ⎿  Read lua/floating-claude/state.lua (3 lines)

● Line 12 sets up an empty slot for the corner notification's timer. Lines 13–14 are the comment for the next field, which stores where you last dragged the
  notification (row and column) for the rest of the session, with nil meaning the bottom-right corner.
